summary: Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1931 and later as Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), where he also taught (~1985–1993), before becoming a professor at Koyasan University around 2002.
Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura is an Indology scholar who earned a PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002) studying under Toshifumi Goto, Hirofumi Isoda, and Shinkan Murakami. She later held a post as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University.

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff, and teaches at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2015).
Naomichi Nakada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya and doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist educated at the University of Tokyo and University of Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and became director of Toyo Bunko in 1974.

Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions as an encouraging researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo. He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple from circa 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1971).
Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indology scholar who served as Librarian (adhyaksha) at the Sarasvati Bhavana Library (attested 1932) and Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indology and history scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and the University of Calcutta (PhD 1985). He held posts at Kobe University, Toyo Bunko, CEACS, and served as Professor at Tokyo (1984–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).

Natalie Depraz is a philosopher educated at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre. She has held posts at Sorbonne, University of Rouen Normandy (professor since ~2006), and Galatasaray University (2020), founding the Rouen School of Phenomenology in 2018.
Natalie Gummer is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University (attested 2001) and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.
